function: above_phy, p. 6: the learned multi-agent attention-enhanced QMIX performs only channel access mode selection (access control); beamforming, RIS phase shifts and time allocation are optimized by AO, not learned.
notes: Exclude, above_phy (first code that applies). The method contains a learned component, so no_learning does not apply, but that component acts above the physical layer. p. 6: "the outer-loop learning for access control and the inner-loop optimization for transmission control" (same split in Fig. 2, p. 6). p. 7: "ai is the UD-i’s access control" [strategy]; "Apart from the binary access mode selection, the other transmission control variables are continuous and efficiently tractable by the inner-loop optimization". The learned action picks, per device, energy harvesting, NOMA transmission, or RIS-assisted relaying (p. 5), a channel access and scheduling decision. BS transmit and receive beamforming and RIS phase shifts are solved by SDR with a rank-one penalty and SCA inside an AO loop (pp. 8-10, Algorithm 1), and time allocation by a linear program (p. 10), so no physical-layer decision is learned jointly with the access decision. Borderline point for the reviewer: the learned RIS-assisted relaying mode decides which device-mounted RISs reflect; counting that on/off choice as RIS configuration would let the work pass this check into area 3. Title and DOI on p. 1 match the PDF.
